Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Body, health & movement

bearded adjective

also with a beard

classical

Cic. N. D. 1.83: Jovem semper barbātum, Apollinem semper imberbem (Lewis & Short)
Plaut. Men. 854: barbātum, tremulum Tīthōnum

barbātus, barbāta, barbātum

declension

having a beard

Its opposite is imberbis. In the poets also “grown up”, and of the old Romans, who did not shave.

Examples

  • dīcere licēbit Jovem semper barbātum, Apollinem semper imberbem

    one may say that Jupiter is always bearded and Apollo always beardlessCic. N. D. 1.83 (Lewis & Short)

See also beard, shave, moustache.

SourcesLewis & Short: barbatus

Plautus, Menaechmi 854.
